\newlabel{M:fig:family-census-tree}{{10}{60}{Anatomy of the $400$ scored accepted source commits of the public competition, through 18 July (\#883--1294): each is placed in one primary family (level~1) and, where the family subdivides, one change-type (level~2), by an audit of its actual \texttt {git show} diff (not its commit subject or lever name, which are frequently unreliable). Blue nodes are the nine families of \Cref {sec:anatomy}---six named for familiar classical compiler categories and three (uncompute strategy, register/scratch allocation, and \emph {codec/encoding}) distinguished here because reversibility changes their resource and proof obligations; amber nodes are the two residual buckets outside the taxonomy---the \emph {verifier search} for a clean Fiat--Shamir nonce (not a circuit optimization), and neutral churn. Counts are by \emph {accepted source commit}, not by score improvement: these scores are absent from the git history but are recovered from the public leaderboard (\Cref {sec:supp-census}); read as counts, the tree measures how \emph {often} a move was primary, not how much it saved; roughly half of these commits additionally touch the Fiat--Shamir nonce as an accompaniment, counted under their circuit change rather than as verifier search. Only competition submissions are counted here; the earlier pre-competition development commits, where most techniques are first documented, are excluded. The prospective representation/coordinate-change family (\Cref {sec:anatomy}), characterized only in that pre-competition research, has no landed competition instance and so no node. The four unscored \texttt {DUMMY\_TOFFOLIS} bootstrap commits (accepted but never scored) are also excluded, so the tree covers the $400$ scored source commits; the full per-commit ledger, including those four, is \Cref {tab:supp-census}}{figure.caption.55}{}}
